subject: TheraGen reserved GPU qualification & next milestones
body:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Emily Cho <emily.cho@theragen.com>, Carlos Mendes <carlos.mendes@theragen.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: reserved GPU qualification & next milestones

Hi Emily / Carlos —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we all have the same checklist and owners. If I missed anything, please flag.

Call summary (30m)
- Use case: TheraGen wants to migrate high-throughput model inference for document-processing pipelines (OCR post-processing + named-entity extraction) from bursty cloud infra to a reserved, low-noise GPU pool.
- Primary pain points: unpredictable tail latency during business hours, noisy neighbors on shared endpoints, and cost volatility during heavy training/eval periods.
- Business goal: stabilize per-request P95 latency to <120ms for 512-token average jobs, and reduce inference unit cost by ~30% vs current serverless spend.
- Scale target: initially 3 reserved GPUs (NVIDIA H100-equivalent) for production; ability to scale to 12 GPUs over 6–9 months as throughput grows.
- Isolation requirement: strict multi-tenant isolation (no shared tenants), VPC peering with private egress, and audit logs for call traces (PCI-like evidence requested).
- SLA expectations: 99.9% uptime for the reserved pool, with defined rollback and fallback to hosted instances for <100ms warm-failover.

Technical constraints called out
- Model: custom 30B transformer with 8k context, currently FP16. Customer interested in 4-bit quantization testing to reduce memory footprint.
- KV cache sizing: long-lived sessions for document batches; need >48GB KV cache per instance.
- Data residency: US-only region for PII handling; agreed no cross-region fallbacks without prior consent.

Action items (owners / timeline)
1) Redwood to provide: draft SOW and cost estimate for 3-GPU reserved pool + add-on burst policy by EOD Friday (owner: Rishi).
2) Redwood to run a quick latency bench (customer sample prompt set) and share results + recommended quantization profile (owner: Rishi / Infra team) by Wednesday.
3) TheraGen to share: procurement contact + signed NDA copy; confirm internal security checklist items (owner: Kamil).
4) Joint technical call to validate network setup and KV cache sizing (30–45m) — target week of July 5 (owner: Emily / Rishi).

Attachments referenced: Dedicated_SOW_v1.pdf (stub), LatencyBench-results.csv (will contain sample-run traces).

Next meeting suggestion: Wed July 7 at 10:00 AM PT for the technical validation (I can send a calendar invite once Emily confirms).

Thanks — looking forward to moving this to a committed pilot.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0182

-----Original Message-----
From: Emily Cho <emily.cho@theragen.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Carlos Mendes <carlos.mendes@theragen.com>, Kamil Rahman <kamil.rahman@procure.theragen.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 16:01:18 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: reserved GPU qualification & next milestones

Thanks Rishi —

Appreciate the clear summary. A couple of clarifications from our side:
- Scale: the 12-GPU growth path is accurate, but we expect step changes tied to quarterly releases (Q3/Q4). Can you include cost breakpoints for 3 / 6 / 12 GPUs in the estimate?
- SLA: 99.9% is fine for the reserved pool but we need a separate SLA lane for holdout canary traffic during rollout.
- Compliance: Kamil will share TheraGen's security questionnaire. We also need an explicit path for SOC2 evidence and keystore integration.

We've attached our signed NDA in this reply (TheraGen_NDA_signed.pdf). Procurement (Kamil) is on this thread and will coordinate the PO cadence.

Emily
Emily Cho
Head of ML Platforms | TheraGen
emily.cho@theragen.com | (206) 555-4490

-----Original Message-----
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Emily Cho <emily.cho@theragen.com>, Carlos Mendes <carlos.mendes@theragen.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 09:20:05 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: reserved GPU qualification & next milestones

Emily / Carlos —

Attached: Dedicated_SOW_v1.pdf and a first-pass latency benchmark from our test cluster (LatencyBench-results.csv). Notes:
- Benchmarks were run on H100-equivalent nodes with a 30B model proxy; results show median latency 95ms, P95 at 130ms for the sample prompt set. We expect the P95 to drop under 120ms after KV cache tuning and enabling continuous batching in the reserved pool.
- SOW v1 includes: scope (3-GPU pool, private VPC peering, KV cache config), onboarding milestones, rollback/fallback policy, and draft SLAs. Pricing section includes monthly reserved vs. burst rates and a simple growth schedule for 6/12 GPU breakpoints.

Please review and let me know items to redline. I can incorporate procurement language Kamil typically requires.

Attachments (stub):
- Dedicated_SOW_v1.pdf (application/pdf, 152 KB)
- LatencyBench-results.csv (text/csv, 28 KB)

Best,
Rishi

Date: Fri, 02 Jul 2027 10:08:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Post-call recap: reserved GPU qualification & next milestones

Looping in here briefly — saw the SOW and bench. Pricing looks within expected ranges for a pilot. I greenlight internal approval to present the 3-GPU reserved pilot discount at the levels you proposed (Rishi, go ahead and surface the formal discount in the SOW).

Two asks from finance before we hand to procurement:
1) Add a 90-day termination clause with 30-day notice for pilot (to reduce procurement friction).
2) Include a simple usage cap and overage schedule for burst (we can use the same template as last month).

Once those are in, I approve and you can send the final SOW to Kamil / procurement.

Thanks —
Ben Carter
